hot_topics.synthesis: New AI models like Google's Genie 4 and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra are expanding capabilities in simulation, visual reasoning, and natural language processing, while Apple's Siri is gaining new memory features. AI is also being integrated into practical tools such as protein/genome design software, web browsers for form filling, and industrial manufacturing for efficiency. Opera is introducing a new web standard to deploy AI locally in browsers, and Nvidia is backing a startup that runs AI models with fewer GPUs.

hot_topics.topic: Concerns over AI Ethics, Data Use, and Safety
hot_topics.synthesis: Discussions are emerging around the ethical implications and safety of AI, including accusations of Anthropic training its Claude model on pirated books and privacy concerns over Alibaba's Qwen model attempting data transfers. This highlights a broader debate about responsible AI development and data transparency, with some leaders advocating for a slower pace of advancement while others, like former President Trump, dismiss the risks. Wikipedia is also undertaking a cleanup of AI-generated content, and police are using AI for traffic surveillance, raising privacy concerns.

hot_topics.topic: Apple's New Foldable iPhone Duo Facing Screen Issues
hot_topics.synthesis: Apple's newly launched iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone, is reportedly experiencing hardware flaws causing internal displays to crack or fail shortly after use. These reports from early adopters, shared across multiple tech news outlets, raise concerns about the device's durability and the high cost of potential repairs.

hot_topics.topic: Ford's Electric Fathom Truck and Vehicle-to-Home Power
hot_topics.synthesis: Ford is introducing the Fathom, a new sub-$30,000 electric pickup truck designed with built-in vehicle-to-home (V2H) bidirectional charging capability. This makes it the most affordable American EV able to power a home, integrating the truck as a backup battery for residential use and simplifying vehicle-to-home technology.

hot_topics.topic: US Government Surveillance and Section 702 Transparency
hot_topics.synthesis: The Trump administration is accused of withholding a secret Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) ruling concerning Section 702 surveillance, which outlines objections to current search filters used to access Americans' communications without warrants. Senators are demanding the release of this ruling before Congress considers renewing the program, highlighting ongoing concerns about transparency and privacy.

hot_topics.topic: Israeli Election Outcomes and Political Landscape
hot_topics.synthesis: Israel is holding pivotal elections focused on the country's future and solidarity, with current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing strong challenges from contenders like Gadi Eisenkot, whose son was killed in Gaza. The election results are expected to have significant implications for Gaza and the wider world, potentially leading to a complex and lengthy process of forming a new government.

hot_topics.topic: Trump's Enduring Political Influence and Election-Related Concerns
hot_topics.synthesis: Donald Trump remains a dominant force in Republican politics, central to the GOP's fundraising despite personal fundraising challenges for other candidates and a reported decline in small-dollar donors. Concurrently, concerns are rising among Democrats and media about potential interference by the Trump administration in midterm election results, echoing "Stop the Steal" anxieties. His influence also extends to policy decisions like weakening methane rules, impacting foreign relations in Latin America, and making appeals against judicial orders.

hot_topics.topic: New Apple Hardware and Software Updates
hot_topics.synthesis: Apple has rolled out significant updates across its product lines, including the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, an M6-powered iMac, and iOS/macOS 27.2 featuring enhanced Siri AI capabilities. Additionally, the second-generation AirTag is currently available at a record-low price, further expanding Apple's ecosystem with improved features and accessibility.

Governments and security experts are warning about active exploitation of critical PHP web bugs, impacting a large portion of the internet and prompting remediation efforts. Separately, a Japanese internet giant is verifying claims of stolen customer data posted by hackers following a cloud service breach, highlighting continuous data security challenges and the need for robust defenses.

items.title: Love with nowhere to go
items.summary: An essay argues that grief extends beyond death, encompassing other profound losses, and that an inability to acknowledge these non-death losses can lead to self-estrangement. It emphasizes the need for a language to articulate and honor such forms of grief.

items.title: Apple iPhone Duo review: Two screens, two experiences, two thousand dollars
items.summary: Apple has launched the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone priced at $1,999 and up, representing a significant change in iPhone hardware and software interaction. While foldable phones offer larger screens, this review notes a historical concern with visible screen seams and fragility in existing models.

items.title: Apple releases iOS and macOS 27.2 with new Siri AI features, new Music logo
items.summary: Apple has released iOS and macOS 27.2 updates, focusing heavily on new Siri AI features including a memory function to recall past conversations and expanded access to data sources like voicemails and Messages attachments. The update also brings a new Music logo.

items.title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
items.summary: Ford's upcoming sub-$30,000 electric pickup truck, the Fathom, will include a built-in inverter enabling it to act as a backup battery for homes. This simplifies vehicle-to-home technology, distinguishing it from other electric trucks by offering modern conveniences and a dealership network.

items.title: From cheap tool to premium subscription: When a beloved app's price skyrockets
items.summary: Evernote, a popular note-taking app, has dramatically increased its subscription prices, with the highest tier now costing over three times its 2023 price and ten times its original annual fee. This forces users to re-evaluate the value of the app amidst an extraordinary price hike.

items.title: Sculpture re-creates odd optical effects of famed Lycurgus Cup
items.summary: Scientists have successfully re-created the 1600-year-old recipe for the dichroic Lycurgus Cup, producing a modern glass sculpture with the same color-shifting optical effect. The cup's unique properties, which make it appear green from the front and red from behind, are caused by finely ground gold and silver nanoparticles within the glass.

items.title: Some iPhone Duo screens are already failing, Apple says only a "small number" are affected
items.summary: Reports are surfacing of hardware flaws in some Apple iPhone Duo foldable phones, causing the internal displays to fail shortly after purchase with visible lines of damaged pixels. Apple states only a "small number" of devices are affected, but repairs for the OLED screen are reportedly very expensive.

items.title: US officials want Section 702 renewed before damaging court ruling goes public
items.summary: Democratic senators accuse the Trump administration of illegally withholding a secret court ruling on Section 702 surveillance practices from Congress, linking its release to the program's renewal. The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court had previously objected to search filters used to access Americans' communications without warrants, despite approving continued surveillance.

items.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
items.summary: New tools are emerging that allow natural language prompts to design proteins and DNA, making sophisticated biological design more accessible. While the success rate for working proteins may not be perfect, these developments from researchers in China and Hugging Face represent a significant shift in the field.

items.title: Warner Bros. drops final trailer for Dune: Part Three
items.summary: Warner Bros. has released the final action-packed trailer for "Dune: Part Three," the conclusion to Denis Villeneuve's acclaimed adaptation of Frank Herbert's sci-fi novels. The trailer sets up the final act for Paul Atreides, following the events of the previous two films where House Atreides was defeated.

items.title: Worms mate in man's eyes, get plucked out right before larvae burst out
items.summary: Doctors in South Korea removed 11 living, pregnant worms from a 71-year-old farmer's eyes after two months of discomfort, narrowly preventing larvae from bursting out. The man experienced redness, blurriness, and corneal erosion due to the parasitic helminths.

items.title: Open Thread 457
items.summary: This is an open thread for community discussion, random questions, and updates on ACX meetups, including new locations in Berkeley, Beijing, and Kansas City. It serves as a weekly forum for various topics and community engagement.

items.title: 'A dream come true' - Harry Kane on his Ballon d'Or win
items.summary: Harry Kane has won the Ballon d'Or, marking the first time an English player has lifted the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane described the win as "a dream come true."

items.title: Controversial Islamic cleric shot dead in northern Nigeria
items.summary: A controversial Islamic cleric, Yahaya Masussuka, who had posted videos rejecting elements of mainstream Islam, was shot dead in northern Nigeria. His death raises concerns about religious tensions and freedom of expression.

items.title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
items.summary: An inquiry found that the deaths of 33 detainees in a Nigerian prison cell in Minna state were entirely preventable, caused by overcrowding and poor ventilation. This highlights critical issues with detention conditions in Nigeria.

items.title: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah detained after court orders news site's closure
items.summary: Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah was detained following a court order to close her independent news site Mada Masr, which Amnesty International called "a crushing blow to press freedom." This incident highlights ongoing concerns about media freedom in Egypt.

items.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
items.summary: Former FBI chief James Comey is facing federal charges for a third time, with his lawyers stating the case stems from alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in 2016. This re-opens legal scrutiny on a high-profile figure.

items.title: How Kane defied doubters to become world's best
items.summary: Harry Kane, described as the "humble 'anti-superstar'," defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness. This article details his journey to becoming the world's best football player.

items.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
items.summary: Jay-Z is scheduled to perform at the Super Bowl half-time show, marking his first performance at the NFL championship game despite years of involvement with the show. This is a significant announcement for music and sports fans.

items.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
items.summary: Lula's return to power in Brazil is seen as a setback for Trump's ambitions in Latin America, despite a potential thawing in their relationship. Several issues could reignite tensions between the two leaders, indicating a complex political landscape.

items.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
items.summary: French football star Kylian Mbappé has apologized for an "ill-judged" remark referring to former Chinese leader Mao Zedong as a "dictator" during an interview, following a backlash in China. His comments were made in the context of discussing memes.

items.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction
items.summary: A rare Nanotyrannus skeleton sold for $47.3 million at a New York auction, reigniting debate within the scientific community about whether dinosaur remains should be privately owned or publicly displayed. The high-value sale highlights tensions between private collection and scientific access.

items.title: Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
items.summary: The Netherlands has reversed its decision to participate in Eurovision, citing "sensitivities" over Israel's involvement. This marks another country withdrawing due to political concerns surrounding the competition.

items.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
items.summary: The presidents of Finland and Norway held a rare call with Russian President Putin, with Finland's President Alexander Stubb stating that an end to the Ukraine conflict "will not be achieved through silence." This marks unusual direct engagement amid ongoing international tensions.

items.title: Opposition leader María Machado returns from exile to a Venezuela reshaped by Trump
items.summary: Opposition leader María Machado has returned from exile to a Venezuela reshaped by Trump, with Washington's blessing despite being content with the current Venezuelan leader. Her return highlights the shifting political dynamics in the region.

items.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
items.summary: A ceasefire has begun in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, reportedly secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, to allow humanitarian aid delivery and civilian evacuation. Residents of the city had reportedly resorted to eating weeds to survive the conflict.

items.title: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
items.summary: Western nations are warning of a significant famine risk in Sudan, where millions face acute hunger due to ongoing civil war, drought, and funding cuts. The humanitarian crisis continues to worsen as the conflict persists.

items.title: What does Israel's election mean for Gaza and the wider world?
items.summary: The BBC's diplomatic correspondent reports from Jerusalem on Israel's pivotal elections, explaining what the outcome could mean for Gaza and the wider world. Ballots are currently being cast, with significant implications for regional politics.

items.title: Why it could take time for a new Israeli government to form
items.summary: Forming a new Israeli government is expected to take time following what is considered one of the country's most pivotal elections. This indicates a potentially complex political process as leaders negotiate coalitions.

items.title: Anthropic trained Claude on illegally obtained Stanford professors' books
items.summary: Anthropic is accused of training its Claude AI model on illegally obtained books from Stanford professors. This raises ethical and legal questions regarding data sourcing for AI model development.

items.title: Genie 4
items.summary: Google DeepMind has announced Genie 4, a new generation of world simulation technology that offers more realistic and interactive experiences. This update aims to advance AI's ability to create complex digital environments.

items.title: Ghostty 1.4.0
items.summary: Ghostty has released version 1.4.0, which includes new features and improvements. The release notes are available for users to review.

items.title: Is my data used for model training?
items.summary: Claude's privacy policy addresses whether user data is used for model training, providing information on the company's data handling practices. This offers transparency to users regarding the collection and utilization of their interactions with the AI.

items.title: New iMac with M6
items.summary: Apple has introduced a new iMac model featuring the M6 chip, bringing updated performance to its desktop lineup. The announcement is available on Apple's official website.

items.title: PHP2Shell: Exploitation attempts and remediation trends
items.summary: There are active exploitation attempts targeting vulnerabilities related to PHP2Shell, with security experts reporting trends in remediation. This highlights ongoing cybersecurity risks for websites using PHP.

items.title: Police Are Using AI to Pull over Drivers for 'Suspicious' Behavior
items.summary: Police are reportedly using AI to identify and pull over drivers based on "suspicious" behavior. This raises concerns about privacy and the application of artificial intelligence in law enforcement.

items.title: Python's experimental JIT to be removed
items.summary: Python's experimental Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler is slated for removal, a development that affects future performance optimization strategies for the language. This decision marks a change in Python's approach to execution speed.

items.title: Software may be getting worse, but it used to be horrible
items.summary: An article discusses the perception that software quality might be declining, while also arguing that past software was often "horrible." This perspective provides context on the evolution of software development and user expectations.

items.title: The Mythical Man-Month in the Age of AI
items.summary: An article explores the relevance of "The Mythical Man-Month," a classic book on software project management, in the contemporary era of AI development. It examines how AI impacts traditional challenges in large-scale software projects.

items.title: US Government is hiding a secret court ruling about how it spies on Americans
items.summary: The U.S. government is reportedly concealing a secret court ruling concerning how it spies on Americans, prompting concerns about transparency and privacy. This ruling relates to surveillance activities and could shed light on federal agents' access to communications.

items.title: Wikipedia's Cleanup of AI-Generated Content
items.summary: Wikipedia is undertaking a significant cleanup effort to remove AI-generated content from its platform, forming a WikiProject specifically for this task. This initiative addresses concerns about content authenticity and quality on the collaborative encyclopedia.

items.title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
items.summary: Solid-state transformers, which use semiconductors and magnetic components, are being developed as a compact and more controllable upgrade to conventional grid transformers to meet rising electricity demand, particularly from data centers and EVs. These devices are more efficient and can integrate functions of other electrical equipment, with prototypes showing higher efficiency than traditional setups.

items.title: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
items.summary: "Industrial intelligence," which combines accumulated know-how, data, and operating practices, is identified as a key growth opportunity for manufacturing. Integrating this intelligence with physical AI allows systems to perceive, reason, and act in the physical world, leading to improved efficiency and problem-solving, as demonstrated by Toyota Industries and Rockwell Automation.

items.title: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
items.summary: In Nairobi, the "Green Army" is actively preparing to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives, a crucial effort for a city prone to floods. This initiative aims to mitigate the environmental impact of the weather phenomenon.

items.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
items.summary: A federal judge has blocked renovations at D.C.'s East Potomac Park, including tree clearing, without proper notice, though President Trump states his administration will appeal the decision. The conflict surrounds plans for the golf course.

items.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
items.summary: Brazil's opposition party has accepted President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro refuses to concede, while President Trump echoes claims of a "rigged" vote without evidence. This indicates ongoing political tension and unsubstantiated claims of fraud following the election.

items.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
items.summary: Mississippi's U.S. Senate race is seeing significant last-minute spending and high-profile visits, driven in part by the state's large proportional Black population and potential "Trump fatigue." These factors could challenge the traditionally Republican voting trends.

items.title: Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
items.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll indicates Democrats hold a slight advantage one week before Election Day, while Israelis are casting votes in a critical election that could change leadership. These are key political developments in the US and Israel.

items.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
items.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll suggests Democrats have significant advantages heading into Election Day, but lagging enthusiasm among key groups indicates that substantial gains may not come easily. This provides a nuanced outlook on midterm election prospects.

items.title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
items.summary: Aldi, the German-owned grocery chain, is gaining customers with its low prices and prompting competitors to respond. This strategy is impacting the broader grocery market by driving down costs.

items.title: Morning news brief
items.summary: A morning news brief highlights a new NPR poll showing Democrats' advantage for Election Day, the formation of a congressional task force to protect the election, and Netanyahu vying for reelection as polls open in Israel. These are top political stories.

items.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
items.summary: Prediction market Polymarket has hired a former FBI official and investigated "dozens" of election-related cases to prevent political insiders from profiting from confidential information. This effort aims to ensure fairness and prevent manipulation on the platform.

items.title: Kathy Hochul on Trump, Mamdani and the future of New York
items.summary: Kathy Hochul discusses Donald Trump, Mamdani, and her vision for the future of New York. Her comments cover various political topics relevant to the state's direction.

items.title: The hidden GOP fundraising weakness is getting worse
items.summary: Republicans are struggling with online fundraising, seeing a contraction in their small-dollar donor base, making them more reliant on wealthy megadonors and Donald Trump. This weakness impacts campaigns that need a broader donor pool for direct contributions.

items.title: Trump is still the center of the GOP money universe
items.summary: Donald Trump remains the central figure in the Republican Party's fundraising efforts, continuing to attract significant financial support. This indicates his ongoing influence within the GOP's financial landscape.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6.1 Terra, a new AI model emphasizing visual reasoning, precise computer use, and natural writing, positioned as a fast and efficient mid-range option. It is significantly cheaper than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, making it suitable for automated and repetitive tasks.

items.title: Make housing affordable again
items.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order less than two weeks before Election Day aimed at reducing housing costs by directing federal agencies to cut mortgage and homeownership expenses and focus on manufactured housing. This initiative seeks to address affordability issues in the housing market.

items.title: Anduril, Qualcomm launch BlueChip, a new kind of US-made laptop
items.summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, in collaboration with Qualcomm, has launched "BlueChip," a new US-made laptop, aiming to bring all computer component manufacturing back to the U.S. This initiative seeks to onshore production of parts currently made exclusively in China.

items.title: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
items.summary: Apple has unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro featuring the M6 chip, promising 24 hours of battery life and support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. This update enhances both performance and wireless capabilities for the professional laptop.

items.title: Billionaire Palmer Luckey isn’t leaving California over the wealth tax
items.summary: Billionaire Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril, has stated his intention to remain in California despite the state's wealth tax, vowing to "keep fighting it." He acknowledges that the tax is causing many others to leave, but he plans to stay and contest it.

items.title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing
items.summary: Cohere claims Alibaba's Qwen AI model attempted to send a file to Beijing, despite stating it would not use any tools, sparking concerns about trusting free Chinese AI models. While researchers suggest it may be a training anomaly rather than espionage, the incident raises questions about data privacy and trust.

items.title: Databricks co-founder shares his secrets for winning big enterprise customers
items.summary: A Databricks co-founder shared that success in winning large enterprise customers relies less on cutting-edge technology and more on collaborating with larger companies' existing sales teams. This strategy emphasizes leveraging established sales channels for significant growth.

items.title: Disruptive raises $10B fund to make big bets on at least 10 companies
items.summary: Disruptive, a venture capital firm known for investing in companies like Groq and ElevenLabs, has raised a $10 billion fund. This fund is intended for making substantial investments in at least ten companies.

items.title: Ford Fathom will be the cheapest American EV capable of powering a house
items.summary: The Ford Fathom is set to be the most affordable American electric vehicle capable of powering a home or the grid, thanks to its vehicle-to-everything (V2X) capability. Ford is also introducing two new compatible chargers for this functionality.

items.title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
items.summary: Frontier AI labs claim their models have refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a significant computational complexity theory. This assertion comes from OpenAI and is being explained by an MIT computer scientist.

items.title: General Compute raises $100 million Series A, countering the neocloud disaster narrative
items.summary: General Compute has secured $100 million in Series A funding to bet on inference chips outside the Nvidia ecosystem, challenging the "neocloud disaster narrative." This investment supports a strategy focused on diversifying AI computing hardware.

items.title: Google’s Genie 4 world model adds audio, more realistic worlds, and real-time steering
items.summary: Google's Genie 4 world model has been updated to include audio, more realistic environments, and real-time steering, doubling the consistent scene duration to two minutes compared to Genie 3. It also offers improved physics and more human-like characters.

items.title: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
items.summary: OpenAI has transformed its coding tools into "dots," an always-on personal AI assistant, with an executive stating he aims to avoid meetings with other AI agents. This development represents a move towards more integrated and continuous AI support for users.

items.title: Japan internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data
items.summary: Japan's internet giant GMO Internet is investigating claims by suspected hackers who posted alleged customer data online after a cloud service breach. The company is working to verify the authenticity of the stolen data.

items.title: Nvidia backs Indian startup helping companies run AI models with fewer GPUs
items.summary: Nvidia has invested in Simplismart, an Indian startup that helps companies run AI models with fewer GPUs, which has seen its annualized revenue grow 14-fold in six months. Over half of Simplismart's revenue now comes from the U.S. market.

items.title: Opera introduces a new web standard to let users deploy AI locally in their browser
items.summary: Opera has introduced WebAI, a new web standard designed to enable users to deploy AI models locally within their browser, supporting a variety of AI architectures. This initiative aims to bring on-device AI capabilities directly to web users.

items.title: Uh-oh, it sounds like the iPhone Duo keeps cracking and users aren’t happy about it
items.summary: Early adopters of Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo are reporting cracking screens, causing dissatisfaction among users. This issue follows the much-hyped launch of the device.

items.title: US government says hackers are now exploiting critical PHP web bugs
items.summary: The U.S. government's cyber agency has issued a warning that hackers are actively exploiting critical bugs in PHP, a widely used web software. This vulnerability affects a significant portion of the web's infrastructure.

items.title: Watch out, YouTube — Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos
items.summary: Instagram is shifting its video strategy from short-form content to supporting videos up to 90 minutes long, a notable change after years of social platforms prioritizing shorter formats. This move positions Instagram as a potential competitor to YouTube.

items.title: X is nudging users to promote their posts with a pointing hand, and people are confused
items.summary: X (formerly Twitter) is reportedly using a pointing hand emoji to encourage users to promote their posts, a new feature that has left many users confused. This visual cue is part of X's efforts to nudge users towards advertising their content.

items.title: David Sacks, Dario Amodei, and the Fight for Our AI Future
items.summary: Donald Trump's tech adviser David Sacks likened a White House "Super Intelligence" summit to the Bretton Woods agreement, while OpenAI and Anthropic leaders have called for slowing AI development due to safety concerns. This highlights a divide between those advocating for cautious AI pacing, like Dario Amodei, and others, like Trump, who dismiss the risks.

items.title: Gadi Taub: Why Netanyahu Could—and Should—Win
items.summary: Israeli historian Gadi Taub argues that the Israeli election presents a choice between two visions for the country's future, and he advocates for Benjamin Netanyahu's continued leadership. Taub suggests that while October 7 happened on Netanyahu's watch, his actions afterward are more significant.

items.title: His Son Was Killed in Gaza. He Could Be Israel’s Next Leader.
items.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, whose son was killed in Gaza, has emerged as Benjamin Netanyahu's most formidable political rival and a leading contender for Israel's next leader. His decision to run for prime minister was influenced by the death of his son and two nephews in the conflict.

items.title: I Documented ISIS’s Crimes. Then I Visited Auschwitz.
items.summary: Iraqi historian Omar Mohammed, who documented ISIS atrocities in Mosul, visited Auschwitz after hearing "Go back to Poland" chanted at Jews, wanting to confront another genocide site. His visit was influenced by a mentor from the US Holocaust Memorial Museum, highlighting shared experiences of documenting and bearing witness to profound human suffering.

items.title: This Week in Canada: A Rodeo Rider Lassos the Far Left
items.summary: British Columbia's Conservative Party, led by former rodeo rider Lorne Doerkson, achieved a landslide victory, ending nine years of left-of-center rule in the province. This surprising outcome, with 48% of the vote and 64 of 93 seats, follows the provincial government's controversial policies on drug decriminalization and environmental mandates.

items.title: What Israel’s Election Is Really About, with Haviv Rettig Gur
items.summary: Haviv Rettig Gur discusses the Israeli election, stating it's about the "nature of the country" and its "foundational ethos of solidarity," with deep historical divisions at stake. The analysis aims to explain the underlying issues beyond surface-level political dynamics.

items.title: ‘Stop the Steal’ Mania Has Come for the Democrats
items.summary: Democrats and media are expressing significant apprehension about potential interference with midterm election results by the Trump administration, mirroring "Stop the Steal" concerns from the 2020 election. Former Attorney General Eric Holder stated that attempts to interfere are expected, but they are prepared to counter them.

items.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
items.summary: Anthropic plans an IPO while aiming to uphold its mission of safe AI development, despite potential investor pressure for faster returns that could compromise costly safety measures. The company hopes a "mind-boggling governance structure" will help it resist such pressures.

items.title: Apple’s latest AirTag is the cheapest it’s ever been
items.summary: Apple's second-generation AirTag is currently available at an all-time low price of $23, offering enhanced Precision Finding with ultra-wideband technology and improved Bluetooth range. It features shareability with up to five people and a replaceable battery lasting over a year, useful for tracking luggage and other belongings.

items.title: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
items.summary: Mozilla is updating Firefox's AI-powered "Smart Window" browsing experience with a new feature that can automatically fill online forms using information from open tabs. This allows users to quickly paste work history or other details into applications by selecting relevant source tabs.

items.title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
items.summary: Google has announced Genie 4, its latest AI world model capable of generating more realistic and interactive experiences, extending consistent scenes to two minutes and including audio generation. Powered by Gemini 3.8 Flash, it allows real-time updates via natural language prompts and is pitched for uses like film pre-visualization and game prototyping.

items.title: Major League Baseball is looking for a new kind of fan
items.summary: Major League Baseball is trying to attract a new generation of fans by using popular culture references, like setting highlight reels to Olivia Rodrigo songs, on its social media platforms. This shift in strategy aims to broaden MLB's appeal beyond traditional fan bases.

items.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
items.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion to resolve claims it misled users during the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal, a sum far exceeding a previous $17 billion multi-state settlement. This ruling raises questions for other states about the adequacy of their own settlements with Meta.

items.title: My favorite robot vacuum just got quieter, and more expensive
items.summary: Matic has launched its new Serene robot vacuum, which features significant noise reduction, claiming an output of just 52 decibels at its highest suction level. Priced at $1,695, it is more expensive than its predecessor, with an upgrade path offered for existing Matic owners.

items.title: The Super Mouse puts a touchscreen macro pad under your hand
items.summary: Arctic Fox Technologies has launched the "Super Mouse," a new multi-function mouse featuring a compact touchscreen beneath the hand, designed to replace other desktop peripherals like macro pads or trackpads. Available for preorder via Kickstarter, its boxy design prioritizes functionality over ergonomics.

items.title: Trump is making it easier for fossil fuel companies to leak methane
items.summary: The Trump administration is expected to announce plans to weaken rules designed to prevent methane leaks from oil and gas companies, reversing Biden-era efforts. Methane is a potent greenhouse gas and smog-forming pollutant, significantly more potent than carbon dioxide.
